advisories.title: Decision 4 puts a permissive body under an 'Owed later work' heading, where the three sibling entries all put an imperative or a consequence
advisories.finding: Decision 4 reads '**Owed later work, not performed here:** a later D-000 MF-6, its own cycle, may add one DR-G* row with owner Protocol + semantic owners whose corpus is hostile-but-well-formed admission inputs covering NT-3 and NT-5.' The heading says owed; the body says may. I compared the branch: D-136 reads 'Owed later MF-6: update DR-133's "no contract exists" clause', D-138 reads 'Owed later work, not performed here: on adoption the live DR-131 status-cell clause becomes stale', and D-144 reads 'Owed later work, not performed here: a D-086 successor names the riding NT classes at G20/G21'. Three of three are imperative or state the consequence that creates the obligation; D-146 alone grants a permission. The result is that the entry does not settle whether anything is owed. A later drafter reading the heading may treat the DR-G23 row as mandated and proceed to a D-002 required-set change; reading the body they may treat it as optional and leave DR-133's leftover open indefinitely.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: No fact is misstated, and the operative content is complete and correct: no row is added, required-now is unchanged, the identifier stays candidate-not-adopted, and NT-3 and NT-5 remain leftover-design. The permissive modality is also arguably the honest one, since nothing compels a DR-G23 row — the coordinator could route these two classes differently or leave DR-133 non-eligible. This is a labelling imprecision, not a false record. I record it because 'owed' has been load-bearing in this corpus, and I charged the converse at D-143.join, where an act was called owed with no instrument creating the obligation.
advisories.repair: Make the modality explicit either way. Either keep the permission and retitle the item — 'Proposed later work, not performed here' — or keep the heading and condition the obligation: a later D-000 MF-6 must add such a row, or an equivalent obligation, if DR-133's leftover-design is to close.

coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Thirteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Custody is clean: 6c720e03 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 95bab60, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, and all seven file pins plus the D-145 commit pin reproduce. The entry records what it says it records. Every claim traces to a field of the artifact — the two classes, the candidate-not-adopted DR-G23 identifier, the owner, the hostile-but-well-formed corpus — with nothing upgraded, and DR-G23 still does not exist in file 08, whose gate table ends at DR-G22. My own verdict is represented exactly, advisory id included; the Codex half I confirmed only as a digest. The readiness recital matches at 4 of 32, every dispatch prohibition is refused in terms, and the COORD-scope refusal that went missing three times earlier in this sequence is present twice. One thing I checked rather than assumed: Decision 1 says the candidate binds NOTHING, which is the phrase I charged at D-145 turn 1. It is correct here. There it contradicted an assertion that the gates now name the classes and departed from D-086's posture for naming artifacts; here it matches the artifact's own binds field and the D-144 branch, and nothing in the entry claims anything took effect. The advisory is that Decision 4 puts a permissive body under an 'Owed later work' heading — 'may add one DR-G* row' — where D-136, D-138 and D-144 all put an imperative or the consequence that creates the obligation. Nothing is misstated and the permission may well be the honest modality, since nothing compels a DR-G23 row; but the entry as written does not settle whether anything is owed, and a later drafter could read the heading as mandating a D-002 required-set change. Either retitle the item or condition the obligation on DR-133's leftover closing. After this entry the DR-133 chain has recorded the contract, the riding measurement, the naming for five classes and the measurement plus candidate obligation for the remaining two; DR-133 stays OPEN, not eligible in kind, not SATISFIED, with gates 2 and 3 not holding.
